title: Pat-a-Cake - A Baking Sing-Along Song for Toddlers
description: Pat it and roll it and pop it in! Clap along while we bake a little cake. #kidssong #nurseryrhyme #toddlersongs #singalong #bakingsong
characters: Three adorable Black toddlers: Zuri, a 3-year-old girl with deep warm brown skin, round afro puffs tied with soft yellow fabric scrunchies, wearing a sunny yellow t-shirt, denim dungaree shorts and white sneakers; Kofi, a 4-year-old boy with medium-deep brown skin, short dark natural curly hair, wearing a blue t-shirt, grey jogger shorts and red sneakers; and Nala, a 3-year-old girl with deep brown skin, neat cornrow braids, wearing a yellow pinafore dress over a white t-shirt, white tights and pink sneakers

lines: Bake me a cake as fast as you can
verses.scene: Two toddlers pat their floury hands together over a low kitchen table dusted with flour and set with a mixing bowl.

lines: Roll it and pat it and pop it in
Now the yummy cake can begin
verses.scene: Small hands roll a ball of soft dough and lower a round cake tin toward a warm, friendly cartoon oven.

lines: Pat and clap along with me
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together in the sunny kitchen, counting on their fingers.

lines: Clap for the cake, so soft and sweet
Clap for the cake we love to eat
verses.scene: A little round cake sits on a plate on the table, and the toddlers clap and cheer around it.

lines: Pat and clap along with me
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together in the sunny kitchen, counting on their fingers.

pd_source.author: Traditional (English)
pd_source.publication: First recorded in Thomas D'Urfey's play The Campaigners (1698); printed as a nursery rhyme in Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book (c. 1744).
pd_source.public_domain: Anonymous traditional text recorded from 1698; long out of copyright everywhere.
pd_source.adaptation: Verse 1 is the traditional couplet verbatim. Verse 2 replaces the traditional 'mark it with B, and put it in the oven for baby and me' — which runs past the 9-word line limit and hangs its rhyme on a single letter — with 'Roll it and pat it and pop it in / Now the yummy cake can begin'. Verse 3 and the hook are NEWLY WRITTEN.

song_style: children's nursery rhyme, cheerful upbeat kids song, cute female child voice, simple very repetitive catchy melody, hand-clapping rhythm, playful, bright, warm
